name: cavemio-time-range-picker
title: Time range picker
description: "Last 15 minutes" for logs, metrics and traces: type 2h or yesterday 14:00–16:00, step by the window, pause live, or drag across a chart to zoom.

cavemio.accessibility:
- The plate is a labelled group of four buttons. The range button opens a dialog whose field is described by the live reading under it; ↓ moves into the quick ranges (a listbox driven by aria-activedescendant), ←/→ move across, Enter applies, Escape closes and returns focus. New ranges are announced in a status region.
- Typed ranges it reads: 15m, 2 hours, last 7 days, past week, today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, last month, since 9, since monday, 14:00–16:00, 9am to 5pm, 22:00–02:00 (past midnight), yesterday 14:00-16:00, 16 oct 09:00 – 16 oct 11:30, oct 12 – oct 14, and ISO dates. Times without a date that haven't happened yet today mean yesterday's.
- parseTimeRange, formatTimeRange, resolveTimeRange and stepTimeRange live in time-range-parse.ts with no React, so a server can read the same ranges from a URL.
- Time brush moves only transforms while you drag and renders nothing; touch keeps vertical page scroll (touch-action: pan-y).
- Reduced motion: no unfolding, gliding, breathing or morphing; the words change in place.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: { type: "relative", duration: 3600000 } · { type: "relative", duration } (the last N ms, live), { type: "since", start } (until now, live) or { type: "absolute", start, end }.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: – · The new range and the times it covers at that moment. Store the range: a relative one keeps moving.

props.name: presets
props.description: TIME_RANGE_PRESETS · Quick ranges. range may be a function of now (Today so far, Yesterday).

props.name: timeZone
props.description: – · Read and show wall-clock times in this IANA zone; the viewer's own by default.

props.name: align
props.description: "end" · Which edge of the plate the panel lines up with.

props.name: label
props.description: "Time range" · Accessible name of the plate.

props.name: TimeBrush
props.type: { start, end, onSelect, minSpan?, snap?, formatTime?, timeZone? }
props.description: – · Wrap a chart whose x axis runs from start to end; onSelect gets the span dragged across. Spans under minSpan (60s) are ignored. snap rounds each edge to one the chart can show (a day boundary on a daily chart), and the band jumps between them while you drag; formatTime(time, edge) writes the edges, e.g. dates instead of hours.

features.title: Ranges that stay live
features.description: “Last 15 minutes” keeps following the clock; Pause freezes it where it is.

features.title: Steps by the window
features.description: ‹ and › move back and forward by the range’s own length, and go live again on reaching now.

features.title: Type any range
features.description: 2h, yesterday, since 9, 14:00–16:00 or 22:00–02:00; the line under the field says what it means before you press Enter.

features.title: Drag to zoom
features.description: Time brush turns a drag across any chart into the range under it.

features.title: Any time zone
features.description: Times are read and shown in the zone you pass, across clock changes.

features.title: Fits a toolbar
features.description: One compact plate that tightens itself on phones.

states.title: live
states.description: A relative range ("Last 1 hour") or one that runs until now ("Today so far") is live: an emerald dot breathes beside Live (2.4s). Pressing it freezes the range where it is; the dot shrinks into a ring and the label morphs to Paused. › is disabled while live.

states.title: step
states.description: ‹ and › move the window by its own length. The label morphs letter by letter ("Last 1 hour" → "Today, 13:20 – 14:20"). Stepping forward into now makes the range live again.

states.title: open
states.description: The panel unfolds from the plate's edge (a clip from the top, 380ms), 6px clear of it, and lines up with its right edge by default. It lives on the page's body, so no card clips it, and it follows the plate when the page scrolls.

states.title: typing
states.description: Each keystroke is read; the line under the field crossfades to what it means ("Yesterday, 14:00 – 16:00 · 2h") and a ↵ appears. Enter applies it. Text it can't read shakes the field and the line turns red with examples.

states.title: quick
states.description: A highlight glides between quick ranges with the pointer or the arrows (220ms); the current range carries a drawn check. Ranges you typed are kept as Recent chips.

states.title: brush
states.description: Time brush: pressing on a chart and dragging draws a band (a scaled fill and two thin line edges, transforms only) with its start, end and length on a tag above it. Release selects that span; the band fades as the chart redraws. Escape cancels.
